who_can_apply: Volunteers must be 16 by the first day of the event (October 3 in 2026).
how_to_apply: New volunteers apply online. If you hear nothing in 30 days, email the Navigator Manager listed on the FAQ page.
notes: You pay your own travel and housing. Most teams stand and walk for long hours outdoors.
duration: Nine morning sessions, from the first Saturday in October to the second Sunday in October.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Uniform pack, event admission and parking, access to the Navigator tent.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 18. You must pass a City of Albuquerque background check before you start.
how_to_apply: Send the online volunteer application. You must also attend a full-day orientation in late May (it was May 30 in 2026). The education team tells you about openings and training.
notes: The page also says 16 years or older in one place and 16 to 18 in another. Costs for the teen are gas and lunch. Shifts are mornings, afternoons or full days. A recommendation letter can be requested after finishing.
duration: At least 40 hours (10 shifts) over seven weeks, June 1 to July 25 (2026 session)
pay_detail: Unpaid. Volunteers get free BioPark admission, discounts and a certificate after 40 hours.

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors ages 16 to 19.
how_to_apply: Apply online in March. Use the BioPark internship page.
notes: Interns work with an animal care team or a plant team. Volunteer coordinator for other teen roles: 505-848-7142.
duration: 8 consecutive weeks, Monday to Thursday 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. (2026: June 1 to July 24)
pay_detail: $5,000 stipend, paid in two halves at week 4 and week 8

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 18 who can pass a City of Albuquerque background check.
how_to_apply: Send in the online volunteer form. Pass a background check. Go to the online open house. Then go to a 2 day orientation in person. Coordinator: 505-848-7142.
notes: Uniform colors are black, brown, khaki or white. Orientation days in 2026 were June 1 and 3 or June 2 and 5.
duration: 2026: June 1 to July 25. At least 40 volunteer hours over an eight-week period.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Free BioPark admission, discounts, behind-the-scenes tours.

who_can_apply: High school students 16 or older who worked as a BioPark Nature Guide or Camp Counselor in a past year. Background check required.
how_to_apply: Call the Volunteer Coordinator at 505-768-3443 about openings. Then apply and pass a background check.
notes: You need earlier BioPark experience. This is a second step after Nature Guides.
duration: One semester. At least 6 hours a week between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Staff can fill out an evaluation form if your school needs one (give two days notice).

who_can_apply: The City page does not state a minimum age. The City's 2026 job fair listing says age 15 and up.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form on the City job site. Then fill out the other forms: a background check, a liability form and a student work form. Anyone under 18 also fills out a drug test consent form. Call a pool to set up an interview with the pool manager. Lifeguards must first pass the City water test.
notes: Lifeguards need a current American Red Cross lifeguard card, plus CPR and First Aid. They must pass the water test. They must do this before the pool manager interview.
duration: Seasonal
pay_detail: Paid. Wage not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Rising high school juniors interested in STEAM careers who can commit 10 to 20 hours a week.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Google Form. Ask a teacher, mentor or parent to send in a recommendation form.
notes: Explora is in Old Town Albuquerque.
duration: Two school years (junior and senior year), 10 to 20 hours a week
pay_detail: Paid internship. Wage not stated.

who_can_apply: Anyone 14 or older.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Volunteer Interest Form.
notes: The volunteer page lists a minimum age of 14.
duration: Ongoing
pay_detail: Unpaid.

who_can_apply: Albuquerque high school students ages 14 to 18.
how_to_apply: Apply in spring. Use the City's Jobs and Internships page. Questions? Call the Educational Initiatives Office at 505-767-5898.
notes: The school-year Job Mentor Program is a 9th to 12th grade elective that earns 0.5 elective credit each semester. The page says interns earn minimum wage.
duration: 7 weeks, up to 25 hours a week
pay_detail: Paid. Wage not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: High school students entering their junior or senior year, and recent graduates, who live in the Albuquerque metro area. The page lists no age.
how_to_apply: Not stated on the page. The City's Youth Connect page lists it with an age of 17 and up, so ask the City before you apply.
notes: Partners named on the page: National Hispanic Cultural Center, Tricklock Theatre, the Public Library, the Balloon Museum and National Institute of Flamenco. The City's list says age 17 and up. The program page has a grade rule. They do not match.
duration: Summer. Length not stated.
pay_detail: Paid. Amount not stated.

who_can_apply: You must be in high school now (freshman to senior). You speak for communities across the City. The page gives no minimum or maximum age. The City's Youth Connect list shows ages 14 and up.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply to MYAC link on the City's Youth Connect page. The page gives no further steps.
notes: Meetings were on Zoom in Sept 2026.
duration: Meets quarterly (Sept, Dec, March, June), first Wednesday, 5:30 to 6:30 p.m.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Free.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17 who are entering 7th through 12th grade.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application linked on the program page. Questions go to the Junior Docent Coordinator, Sioux Rivera. The page says applications are closed.
notes: Unpaid and costs $175. The 2026 session had a required training week June 1 to 5. Contact is the Junior Docent Coordinator listed on the program page. Applications were closed on the page when checked.
duration: Training week June 1 to 5. Work period June 8 to July 31 (2026 session). Typical commitment is two 4-hour shifts a week.
pay_detail: Teens pay a $175 fee. Limited financial help is available.

who_can_apply: Students 16 and older.
how_to_apply: Email the museum's Volunteer Coordinator. The email is on the program page. No separate form is described.
notes: Hours depend on your schedule and the museum's needs. Events named on the page include STEM Day and Nuclear Science Week. The program page does not say whether applications are open. Ask about pay when you write.
duration: At least 12 weeks, full time or part time
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Teens 16 and older can volunteer without a parent or guardian, unless it is a school or group activity. Younger teens and kids must come with an adult.
how_to_apply: Make an account in the online sign-up portal for individuals and families. Pick an open date and time. You get a confirmation email. Groups of five or more fill out a group form at least 3 weeks ahead.
notes: Teens under 16 can join with an adult. Children 8 and up can help in the warehouse with enough adults. Children must be 12 or older to work in the clean rooms. Wear closed-toe shoes and no tank tops.
duration: Shifts are 2 hours long, on weekdays and Saturdays.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer work.

who_can_apply: At least 16 years old. Full-time enrolled high school students with a cumulative GPA of at least 3.0 for research, technical or business jobs (2.5 for clerical or laborer jobs). Some jobs need U.S. citizenship.
how_to_apply: Make a username on Sandia's careers site. Filter for Student jobs. Apply to each internship on its own. A student guide PDF is linked on the page.
notes: Minimum age is 16 per the page. Listings change, so check the careers tool for current postings.
duration: Summer or year round. During the school year, high school students work up to 25 hours a week.
pay_detail: Competitive pay. Amount not stated.

who_can_apply: June option: kids going into 8th, 9th or 10th grade. 8th and 9th graders get priority. July option, where you live on campus: kids going into 11th or 12th grade. Students 16 and older get priority. You need a computer at home or time on site for homework.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Add a personal statement of 400 to 500 words. Ask one math or science teacher to email a recommendation. Email your latest unofficial transcript. Packets that are not complete are not accepted.
notes: The page says room and board might be covered for the July residential option. The program page lists a phone number and email for help with the application.
duration: June option: June 1 to 12. July residential option: June 22 to July 17 (2026 dates)
pay_detail: Tuition, lunches and materials are covered in the June option. Students get a small stipend after finishing. The amount is not stated.

who_can_apply: Volunteers can be as young as 16. The page lists the 16 year minimum for Guest Services at UNM Sandoval Regional Medical Center.
how_to_apply: Fill out the youth application. Then have an interview with the Guest Services team. You also get a tuberculosis screening and go to orientation. The page lists phone numbers to call, one for the Sandoval hospital and one for UNM Hospital.
notes: The page does not list a minimum age for volunteering at the main UNM Hospital, so call that office to ask. The listed steps are for Guest Services at the Sandoval hospital.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer work.

who_can_apply: New Mexico residents with a valid SSN or ITIN (used for payment only). You need an interest in a health career and leadership. The page says juniors and seniors, and also lists rising sophomores.
how_to_apply: Use the online form. You send a student application, a profile with short essays and one recommendation form.
notes: The page does not state an age. It says it focuses on health equity in African American communities and other communities of color. The page still showed the 2026 cycle when checked. Confirm the next dates.
duration: One week (June 15 to 24 in 2026)
pay_detail: A stipend after you finish. The amount is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: The 2024 cohort was youth ages 14 to 22. Rules for 2027 are not posted yet.
how_to_apply: Email programs@workingclassroom.org to get on the list for the 2027 program.
notes: Ages and hours come from the first (2024) cohort. Confirm the 2027 rules.
duration: 2024 cohort: 300 hours over 8 months
pay_detail: Paid. Amount not stated.

who_can_apply: Students. Exact ages and residency rules are not stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Call YDI at 505-352-3466 about this program, or 505-977-3216 (Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.), or email ccordova@ydinm.org.
notes: Only five young people are hired each summer, so it is very small. Ask YDI about the age rule.
duration: June to mid-August
pay_detail: Paid summer employment. Wage not stated.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 24. Residents of Albuquerque and Bernalillo County. Other rules not stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Email youthbuild@ydinm.org. Office: 3411 Candelaria Rd. NE, Suite D, Albuquerque.
notes: The page calls this the final class, so check that a cohort is still open.
duration: not stated
pay_detail: Pay or stipend not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 25. Each youth must register. Parents do not need to register.
how_to_apply: Register on the fair page for the youth who will attend.
notes: The 2026 page listed jobs by the youngest age. Aquatics aide and lifeguard: 15 and up. Community center recreation leader: 16 and up. Library teen volunteer: 13 to 17, a younger age range than the fair's 14 to 25 invitation. BioPark education volunteer: 14 and up. Dates are for the 2026 fair.
duration: One day
pay_detail: Event is free. Jobs listed there are paid; pay not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 24 who want to build skills, get work experience, or start a career. The program page does not list other rules or the counties served.
how_to_apply: Call 303-636-1260 and leave a voicemail. Or fill out the Support Assessment Form on the Connecting Colorado website. You can also use the Training Interest Form on the program page.
notes: Arapahoe/Douglas Works! has its main office in Centennial. Ask which county rules apply to you. Douglas County teens 15 to 17 can also look at the DCYEP program.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Teens. The page does not list exact ages. The library teen section is for ages 12 to 18.
how_to_apply: Use the Teen Volunteer Application on the page. The page lists drop in volunteer events at Koelbel and Smoky Hill libraries.
notes: Each branch Teen Advisory Board meets monthly to talk about trends and plan events.
duration: Semester and summer volunteer options
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Youth ages 8 to 18. Your local Extension office helps you join.
how_to_apply: Call your local Extension office. Then make a profile to join as a youth member.
notes: Also open to younger kids; teen parts are the leader roles. State programs listed include a teen leadership group, shooting sports, STEM projects and a camp on 55 acres of pine forest. Dates were not posted on the program pages.
duration: Ongoing
pay_detail: Not stated on the page. Ask your county office about fees.

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 9 to 12. No minimum GPA is required, but the page says students should show a GPA of 2.7 or higher.
how_to_apply: The program page does not explain the steps. Call 480-727-4948 or use the contact details on the program page.
notes: Students must stay on campus for the whole program. Meals are provided. Next dates are not stated on the program page.
duration: One week on the ASU Tempe campus
pay_detail: Free for all students. There is no cost to apply.

who_can_apply: Students entering grade 11 or 12. No minimum GPA is required, but the page recommends a GPA of 2.7 or higher.
how_to_apply: The program page does not explain the steps. Call 480-727-4948 or use the contact details on the program page.
notes: This is a residential program on the ASU campus. The deposit is not refunded. Next dates are not stated on the program page.
duration: Four days on the ASU Tempe campus
pay_detail: Accepted students pay a $50 deposit that is not refunded. The page lists no other fees.

who_can_apply: Current high school juniors and seniors. You need a 3.25 unweighted GPA and A or B grades in high school math and science. You must qualify for Arizona in-state tuition and have lived in Arizona for the last 2 years.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. You will need financial information from a parent or guardian. Upload a one page personal or career statement. Upload an unofficial high school transcript. Have one recommender send a letter on school letterhead.
notes: The program page lists 2027 dates. Its Spanish section shows 2026 dates for the first and last program days, so confirm the dates with the program.
duration: About 6 weeks. The 2027 program is June 6 to July 16.
pay_detail: Free for students in 2026: tuition, room and board, and class materials. The 2027 page lists no fee.

who_can_apply: Arizona high school juniors. Picks look at leadership. They look at community service, grades, and family income. They also ask if you are first in your family to go to college.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. A recommendation is optional. A teacher can write it. So can another person who works in education. It uses an online form.
notes: The page names both a 2026 application and a summer 2027 group. Confirm the year and deadlines with the program at 480-965-5187.
duration: Online June 14 to 18, 2027, then a Tempe campus visit on June 21, 2027
pay_detail: Free to students who apply and are selected.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17. First time teens must send a reference letter from an adult who is not family (teacher, coach, neighbor and so on).
how_to_apply: Apply online when positions are announced in January. Attach a reference letter if it is your first year. Sign up for the email or text updates on the page.
notes: The pay numbers on the page are labeled 2025, so 2027 wages may be different. Contact: youthcorps@bouldercounty.gov, 303-678-6104. Office: 5201 St Vrain Road, Longmont, CO 80503.
duration: Summer. The 2025 staff dates were June 2 to August 8.
pay_detail: 2025 wages for teen Corpsmembers: $16.54 per hour (1st year), $16.96 (2nd), $17.38 (3rd), $17.82 (4th). Team Leader jobs pay more.

who_can_apply: Teens who live in the City of Boulder. The page does not list ages, grades or the application steps.
how_to_apply: The page does not say how to apply. Use the Youth Opportunities Program page to contact staff.
notes: The same page says the city will not host paid youth internships for 2026 to 2027 and possibly beyond. The page also links a list of local youth leadership programs and a youth volunteer booklet.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Pay is not stated.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 18. No experience is needed.
how_to_apply: Buy a ticket from the link on the program page. Email sumafriends@suu.edu for a Friends of SUMA member discount code.
notes: Supplies are paid for by Cedar City RAP Tax funds. Contact the museum at suma@suu.edu.
duration: 4 days, 12:30 to 4 p.m. (June 16 to 19 in 2026)
pay_detail: $25 per ticket. All supplies are included. Friends of SUMA members get a discount.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 18. You must have finished 8th grade and be enrolled in high school.
how_to_apply: Register and pay online by picking your age group and camp. Within 5 business days you get an email with papers to fill out before camp. Questions: stemsummercamps@suu.edu.
notes: Camps run at both SUU and Southwest Tech. The program page says registration opens in January. Each camp closes when it is full or about two weeks before it starts. All paperwork must be finished before the first day of camp.
duration: Camp lengths vary. See the camp calendar.
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the program pages. You pay at online registration.

who_can_apply: Age 15 and older. The page says you need consistent availability and a year-round commitment, including during the school year.
how_to_apply: Use the View open positions link on the city jobs page. The page also links to a separate certification and training page.
notes: Not stated on the program page whether a work permit is needed. Pay may have changed since January 2025.
duration: Peak season May to July: 20 to 40 hours a week. August to April: 5 to 20 hours a week.
pay_detail: Lifeguard I starts at $17.79 per hour. Lifeguard II (Swim Instructor) starts at $18.67 per hour. These rates are listed as of January 2025 on the program page.

who_can_apply: Age 16 or older. A Teen Application is on the page.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Application on the page or call (480) 256-7086. Steps are an interview, a health check and a background check (3 to 4 weeks). You also need shot records and a TB test. Then you go to orientation.
notes: Min age is 16 for all volunteers. The page does not give a teen age cap.
duration: At least 6 months and 100 hours, one 4-hour shift a week
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 17 at the Hamilton and Basha branches. Ages 13 to 17 at the Sunset and Downtown branches. You can apply to only one branch.
how_to_apply: Pick one branch and read its dates. Fill out the linked application form. If there is no link, there are no openings. Watch for confirmation emails, then attend the mandatory overview or training.
notes: Submitting an application does not guarantee a spot. The program is not a good fit for teens who will miss 2 or more shifts.
duration: One set shift each week for a semester, quarter or summer
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Grades 9 to 12 for the high school tracks (the program also has a middle school track for grades 6 to 8). There is an application and one or two interviews.
how_to_apply: Pay the $25 application fee while the window is open. Then fill out the online form. Then interview. High school applicants may have 2 interviews.
notes: The page says a $25 application fee is non-refundable. Summer programs are tuition based and the page does not state an amount. The page does not give winter session dates. Contact: 719-424-7822.
duration: June 1 to August 8, 2027
pay_detail: Tuition based. The amount is not stated on the page. There is also a $25 application fee that is not refunded.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 16 and 17 use the Youth Volunteer Application. The page lists no opportunities for anyone under age 16.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Youth Volunteer Application on the page. If you have a question, you can send an email to ClarkVolunteer@SaltLakeCounty.gov.
notes: Court ordered service is 18 and older only.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Community clubs are open to youth ages 8 to 18, based on your age on December 31 of the enrollment year. Ages 5 to 7 join Cloverbuds.
how_to_apply: Find your county Extension office and pick a project. Then join on the 4-H Online site. You make a family profile, pick a club and choose projects.
notes: Also open to younger kids; teen parts are the leader roles. Call or email your county Extension office before you start to join online.
duration: Ongoing
pay_detail: Not stated on the state page. Some projects like horse or livestock cost more. Ask your county office.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 18. You complete an application, an interview and a health screening before you start.
how_to_apply: Apply online, then an interview and a health screening.
notes: You can get volunteer credit for scholarship applications. The page does not say which hospital sites take teens. Ask when you apply.
duration: Full-year or summer; about 3 hours per week
pay_detail: Unpaid. Two $2,500 scholarships are given each year to outstanding junior volunteers.

who_can_apply: Students in school ag education programs. No age or grade limits are stated on the page.
how_to_apply: Ask your school's agriculture teacher about an FFA chapter. Use the Chapters page to find one. The Become a State Officer page explains the state officer role.
notes: The Colorado FFA Foundation helps the group, CSU Ag Education and ag teachers. Dates and fees were not on the program pages.
duration: School year
pay_detail: Not stated on the program pages. Ask your ag teacher about dues.

who_can_apply: Young people ages 14 to 24 per the Denver city page. No income rules. You must show proof of age and U.S. citizenship.
how_to_apply: Visit any Workforce Center in Colorado to register. Bring proof of age and U.S. citizenship.
notes: The Denver page and the Jefferson County workforce page both say ages 14 to 24. The state page (cdle.colorado.gov/jobs-training/youth/gsjh) would not load. If you are 14 or 15, call your local Workforce Center to check the age rule.
duration: Summer season
pay_detail: The service is free. The jobs it lists set their own pay.

who_can_apply: Rising high school juniors and seniors who are at least 16 during camp.
how_to_apply: Apply online; the 2026 page lists a waitlist form. Questions: innohub@mines.edu.
notes: The page blocked our reader, so it was read through a page summary tool. Confirm the cost and dates on the Mines page.
duration: One week, 9 AM to 4 PM. 2026 sessions: July 13 to 17 and July 20 to 24.
pay_detail: $850, lunch included. Bring a laptop if you can; loaners are available.

who_can_apply: High school students across Colorado Springs. The page does not list ages or a deadline.
how_to_apply: Download the form on the city page. Send it as shown. Email ira.cronin@coloradosprings.gov with questions.
notes: A news story said under 18 students need a parent signature. That detail is not on the city page, so ask the contact.
duration: Meets once a month
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Anyone at least 14 years old. A background check is needed if you are 18 or older.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now link on the page. Call 719-319-3678 or email volunteer@spacefoundation.org with questions.
notes: You can apply while the museum is closed. The museum plans to reopen in January 2027.
duration: At least two shifts a month, Tuesday through Saturday
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Ages depend on the job: 10 and up for Junior Docent at Rock Ledge Ranch, 13 and up for Spray Ground Assistant, Teen Volunteer and Therapeutic Recreation Discovery Camp roles, and 15 and up for Junior Park Docent at Garden of the Gods and Junior Docent at the Pioneers Museum.
how_to_apply: Register on the page for the job you want. Junior Park Docent at Garden of the Gods signs up by email to gardenofthegods@coloradosprings.gov. Some jobs need an interview and training.
notes: Junior Docents at the Pioneers Museum earn a $300 Education Stipend at the end of the summer if they do at least 40 hours. Teens ages 12 to 15 can only volunteer from 7 am to 7 pm in the school year, and until 9 pm in summer. North Cheyenne Canon teens must finish the free online Leave No Trace 101 course.
duration: Several weeks. Hours differ by job.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 19. You go to a Tribal or Colorado school (online or charter too). Or you are in a home based, high school equivalency or diploma program.
how_to_apply: Apply online when it opens in spring 2027. Contact COYAC to get a notice when applications open.
notes: The COYAC site blocked our page reader, so this was read through a page summary tool. The retreat for the current group is August 29 to 30, 2026 in Denver; the Day at the Capitol is March 1, 2027.
duration: Two year term. Monthly virtual meetings on the second Thursday, 7:45 to 9:15 PM.
pay_detail: Unpaid. The page says lodging and meals are provided at the retreat and travel money is available for the Capitol day.

who_can_apply: High school students who are 16 by June 2, 2027, with no exceptions. It is a commuter program with no housing.
how_to_apply: Apply online. Admission is competitive. Payment is due when you accept. Contact Steven Denham (email link on the page).
notes: No refunds after you enroll. Students match with CU Boulder mentors in May and at orientation on June 2, 2027. Poster session July 30, 2027.
duration: June 2 to July 30, 2027; 15 to 20 hours a week
pay_detail: The page does not post the cost yet. Limited scholarships for students with financial need; say so on the application.

who_can_apply: Open to all high school students, including rising 9th graders. Classes at CU Anschutz Medical Campus are for grades 10 to 12 only.
how_to_apply: Sign up online through Science Discovery when the next season opens.
notes: The same page lists STEM Pathfinders (two weeks, bioscience June 1 to 12, 2026, engineering July 13 to 24, 2026) for the 2026 season. Check the price and 2027 dates on the program page.
duration: One week per class. The 2026 classes ran June to July.
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Ninth graders through high school juniors. You must be a first-generation college student (neither parent finished a 4 year degree). You must attend a target high school. You need at least a 2.5 GPA (freshmen without a GPA are asked to apply). You also need one more thing listed on the page.
how_to_apply: Call or email the program manager first. Norma Marquez, 303-315-7070, PCDP@ucdenver.edu.
notes: The 5 week summer program has college credit classes (ENGL 1020 or ENGL 1010) and fast track math.
duration: Multi-year. Summers: 2 weeks after 10th grade, 5 weeks after 11th grade.
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Ages 12 to 14 or ages 15 to 17, depending on the workshop. Your teen must be the right age by the first day.
how_to_apply: A parent or guardian registers online and pays. You need health and emergency contact details. All sales are final.
notes: Costs money. The 2026 scholarship applications are closed. The Story in Focus workshop is full and has a waitlist, according to the program page.
duration: One week, 9:30 am to 3:30 pm
pay_detail: $450 for museum members and $500 for nonmembers for a full-day workshop. One full scholarship is offered per camp.

who_can_apply: Current high school students, rising freshmen through graduating seniors. You volunteer once a week in June and July. You do at least one shift at Plains Conservation Center or Chatfield Farms.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the summer window opens. Questions: volunteer office email on the program page.
notes: Also on the page: Junior Counselor Program for ages 13 to 15 (1 full week of camp, Monday to Friday 8:30 to 4:30). Also Gardens Teen Leaders, a school year group for teens who finished the summer program. The page gives no exact ages for the summer program. It only says high school.
duration: Once a week, June to July
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Students ages 14 or older. You must be in high school or in a college undergraduate program.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the application reopens. All required documents must be in by the deadline.
notes: Denver Health is at 777 Bannock Street, Denver. Students who cannot shadow can look at the MC2 internship (rising juniors).
duration: Short shadowing experiences
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Current high school sophomores who go to school in the Denver metro or Colorado Springs area and are legally allowed to work in the U.S. You start at the beginning of junior year. No exceptions to the rules.
how_to_apply: One form is used for all sites. A team reads your essays and your GPA. They also look at what you do, what you do for your town, how much you need money help, and 1 recommendation.
notes: Sites are Denver Health and Children's Colorado at Anschutz in Aurora. Others are in Broomfield, Highlands Ranch and Colorado Springs. Contact marisa.valeras@dhha.org. Or call 303-602-2685.
duration: Junior and senior years; 100 to 120 hour paid internship in junior year
pay_detail: Paid internship. The hourly rate is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Denver residents ages 14 to 21 who have a job or a job offer when they apply. The job does not have to be in Denver. Self-employed teens and unpaid interns are not eligible.
how_to_apply: Apply online during the open window with a job or job offer. If chosen (first 2,000 eligible applicants in 2026), watch 10 money videos, send proof of 100 hours and a W-9. Under 18: a parent signs the W-9.
notes: The city does not give you a job. You must already have one. This is a bonus program, not a job. The 2026 page lists job fairs (March, April, May 2026) and says youthworks@denvergov.org and (720) 337-9675 for job help. Look for 2027 fairs in spring.
duration: Work 100+ hours between March 1 and August 14 (2026 cycle)
pay_detail: $250 retention bonus after the program ends.

who_can_apply: Sophomores or juniors (the page ties this to the 2025-2026 school year). Ages 14 to 17 during the internship. You must be free Monday to Friday for a full session. It is for high schoolers from underserved or underrepresented communities or schools.
how_to_apply: Apply online when it opens. Pick your top two tracks and a session, and give your household income and size. No transcript or recommendation is needed.
notes: The museum site blocked our regular reader, so this was read through a page summary tool. Out of state students can apply if they are at the museum for the whole program. Housing is not provided. RTD buses are free for riders 19 and younger. Phone 303-370-6478.
duration: Three weeks. 2026 sessions: early June to late June, or early July to early August.
pay_detail: $1,803 per session in 2026. The page says it is to cover expenses, not wages.

who_can_apply: You must be at least 15 when you apply and by the last day of the training class.
how_to_apply: Apply on the city job site. Next is a short phone interview with the water team. Then take the free lifeguard class (you pass a swim pre-test first). Last is city hiring and onboarding.
notes: The pay and steps were read through a page reader, so confirm the pay on the city job posting. The page says the city needs early morning and daytime guards who can work year-round.
duration: Year-round and seasonal schedules
pay_detail: $19.29 per hour for new lifeguards. Red Cross certification is free if you will work for the city.

who_can_apply: For the free youth meals volunteer job, you must be at least 15 years old, finish an application and pass a background check.
how_to_apply: Email andrea.garcia@denvergov.org to start. Send the online application and any documents you need through Engage Denver. Send questions to Volunteers.Recreation@denvergov.org.
notes: The page says all volunteers must be at least 15, finish an application and pass a background check. It also lists other jobs, like park clean-ups and mountain park projects. It gives no age rule for those.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: High school students. The program page does not list an age range. About 40 to 50 teens take part.
how_to_apply: The program page does not list the steps. Applications open January to March 2027. Questions go to acalvo@platteforum.org or 303-893-0791.
notes: Orientation is each August. Interns stay for one year.
duration: One year, and you can stay up to 4 years. School year: Saturdays, 3 hours. Summer: 3 days a week, 5 hours a day.
pay_detail: Hourly stipend of $11 to $15. Interns also get therapy, tutoring, groceries, and art supplies.

who_can_apply: Middle and high school students from across Denver. The page lists no age or grade cutoffs. Teens under 18 need a signed parent consent form.
how_to_apply: Fill out the TAB interest form. Then follow up with the branch you want to join.
notes: Meetings are in person or online at some branches. The program runs only in English right now. Questions: tab@denverlibrary.org.
duration: Meetings follow the school calendar. They may be weekly, every other week, or monthly.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Snacks are provided.

who_can_apply: Teens must be 14 or older to apply.
how_to_apply: Look at the page to see what is open. If you have questions, email volunteers@denverlibrary.org.
notes: The main volunteer page says most roles are for adults 18 and older, but teen roles exist. Positions fill up, so email the volunteer office to ask when more open.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: 4-H and FFA youth. Ages are not stated on the page. See the 2027 4-H and FFA Eligibility Guidelines linked there. Each state team arranges its own travel.
how_to_apply: Register online. Upload the State Authorized Official form and youth consent forms. Pay by check made out to CSU Extension (no credit cards). Questions: Joy Bauder, CSU 4-H.
notes: The page says all payments are due Dec 30, 2027, which looks like a typo for 2026. Ask Colorado 4-H. Contests also include horse hippology and horse bowl.
duration: January 6 to 9, 2027
pay_detail: $175 per contest if you register by Nov 16, 2026. $250 from Nov 17 to Dec 1. Adults 18 and up: $50. Hotel is extra (Renaissance Denver listed at $129 a night).

who_can_apply: Lifeguard, swim instructor and aquatic jobs: age 15 or older. Part-time camp counselor: age 16 or older and some experience with kids. Full time day camp leader: age 18 or older.
how_to_apply: Go to the summer jobs page. To see all locations, type LIFEGUARD in the search box on that page.
notes: Lifeguards need American Red Cross or YMCA lifeguard certification and CPR-AED. The Y offers lifeguard training. It reimburses the training cost after 3 months of employment. The page does not show a year, so check the jobs search for current openings.
duration: Summer
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Douglas County residents ages 15 to 17, or ages 18 to 25 with a minor in the household. The minor does not have to be related to you. You need U.S. citizenship or lawful presence. Household income must be $75,000 a year or less.
how_to_apply: Use the interest form linked on the program page to see if you are eligible. Virtual information sessions are held about three times a month. You can also call 720-874-5130 or text 720-853-1837.
notes: Only for Douglas County residents. The office is in Centennial, south of Denver. Other help includes GED support and tuition help for short job training.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Services are free. Paid internships are offered, but the pay rate is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Students ages 13 to 18. You send audition videos. Composers send three original works.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Upload audition videos and pay the $75 fee. Ask one teacher to email a recommendation. For need-based aid, email a tax form.
notes: This costs money, but scholarships exist. You must meet the Feb 15 date to be considered for them.
duration: Two weeks, June 16 to 29, 2027
pay_detail: Residential $2,850. Commuter $2,000. Commuter PLUS $2,200. There is also a $75 application fee. Almost 70 percent of students get aid.

who_can_apply: Teens who are 14 through 18 by June 9, 2026. You must be able to work legally in the United States and be available Tuesday to Thursday for the whole program.
how_to_apply: Watch the program page for the next application. In 2026, interviews were in April.
notes: You must carry your own gear and tools to the job site. You can miss no more than three days. You must be on time at Jeffco Parks & Open Space headquarters in Golden each workday. The page does not state a county residency rule.
duration: About 6 weeks (June 16 to July 30 in 2026)
pay_detail: $18 per hour (2026)

who_can_apply: Best for ages 14 to 17. Returning youth ages 18 to 21 can take lead roles. The page says the group hires from nearby areas. They include Westwood, Sheridan, NE Park Hill, southern Commerce City, Montbello and NW Aurora.
how_to_apply: Use the "Current Youth Job Openings" link on the Youth Pathways page.
notes: The website moved from groundworkdenver.org to groundworkcolorado.org. The page also lists a GRIT program for ages 18 to 29, which is not for teens.
duration: Seasonal. Some teams are summer only, some run in the school year.
pay_detail: Paid staff positions. The wage is not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17.
how_to_apply: Download the Teen Volunteer Application (PDF on the page), fill it out and return it to the Customer Service desk at one of the four libraries. Questions: (702) 707-2665.
notes: Henderson is next to Las Vegas. Expect a wait at some branches. Ask about parent consent and hours.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 17. You need 2 letters of recommendation, a negative TB test and a TB screening each year. You also go to new volunteer orientation and training.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online Zoo Corps application on the zoo volunteer page. A Zoo Corps description PDF is linked there.
notes: The zoo site blocked our regular reader, so this was read through a page summary tool. Confirm the dates with the zoo volunteer office.
duration: Summer season, June to August. At least one day a week.
pay_detail: Unpaid. No fee is listed on the page.

who_can_apply: High school students in Utah, Nevada, Montana, Idaho or Wyoming. You must be a rising sophomore or junior. You need consent from a parent or guardian.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply for Program button on the page when it opens.
notes: You must attend all 40 hours. A lab kit is mailed to your home. Contact: Monica Salas Jimenez, Monica.Salas@hci.utah.edu, 801-587-7885.
duration: Two weeks, Monday to Friday, 8:30 AM to 12:30 PM Mountain time (2026: July 6 to 17)
pay_detail: Up to $500

who_can_apply: High school students in Idaho, Montana, Nevada, Utah or Wyoming who finished at least freshman year. Rural students are very welcome. You need consent from a parent or guardian.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply for Program button on the page when it opens. Parent consent is required.
notes: It is online only. The program manager is Jill Christian. Her email is Jill.Christian@hci.utah.edu.
duration: Two weeks, Monday to Thursday, 8:30 AM to noon Mountain time (2026: July 13 to 16 and 20 to 23)
pay_detail: Up to $400

who_can_apply: The program page does not list eligibility rules. It says the program aims to reach young learners, including students from rural and frontier areas of the Mountain West. Check the application for the full rules.
how_to_apply: Use the Online Application link on the page. The program manager is Liz Morales. Her email is liz.morales@hci.utah.edu and her phone is 801-581-3088.
notes: Accepted students who finish are accepted back the next summer. High school students should check that they count as advanced seniors.
duration: 10 weeks, 40 hours a week (2026: May 25 to July 30)
pay_detail: Up to $4,000 for 10 weeks (depends on education level). Housing and meals are paid for out-of-state students. Travel help for students outside Salt Lake City.

who_can_apply: The page lists a few volunteer chances for junior volunteers ages 14 to 17. Most volunteers must be 18.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply now button on the page. Call the volunteer office: Salt Lake City 801-662-6560, Lehi 385-531-1560.
notes: The page does not say which sites take junior volunteers or which rules apply. Call first. Immunization proof is required for volunteers.
duration: Typical adult commitment is one shift a week for at least six months. The junior rules are not stated.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12. Ages are not stated on the program page.
how_to_apply: Open the High School Academy application on the program page. It was open until April 30, 2026. Send questions to Mario Garcia, the Program Manager. His email is neomars@nmsu.edu.
notes: The same page lists a STEM Mavericks camp for high school students. It is a two week camp about public safety and disaster relief. Dates and cost are not stated on the program page.
duration: One week (June 1 to 5 in 2026)
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Lifeguards must be 16 at hire. They need lifeguard training, first aid and CPR certification before hire. The page also lists 1 year of lifeguard experience. Student recreation aides must be 16, in high school, a junior or senior, with at least a 2.0 GPA.
how_to_apply: Look for lifeguard and student recreation aide jobs on the city job openings page. You must show proof of age, GPA and school enrollment when hired.
notes: The page says first pick for lifeguard jobs goes to people 18 or older. Lifeguard jobs have drug and alcohol tests under city rules. The same page lists a free after school Teen Connection program for grades 6 to 12.
duration: Part time and temporary for student aides. Hours vary. Lifeguard hours are not stated.
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Teens in Las Vegas. The program page does not give an age or grade range. The registration form asks for your grade, school and a parent signature.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online registration form on the program page. Ask your nearest teen council site for meeting dates and times. Questions: call the city at (702) 229-6113, the contact named on the program page.
notes: The registration form lists councils at several high schools and community centers. Check with the city for the current site list. A parent signs the form. The form says each council has an adult advisor.
duration: Year-round. Meeting days and times depend on the site.
pay_detail: Free. The city's registration form says activities are free of charge. It does not pay teens.

who_can_apply: You must be 15 to take the lifeguard course. Lifeguard, front desk and laborer jobs need you to be at least 16. You must pass a tryout swim and an interview.
how_to_apply: Sign up for the lifeguard class on the city registration site. Then apply online for the Hourly Lifeguard job. Call Municipal Pool at 702-229-6309 or Pavilion Pool at 702-229-1488 to set your tryout swim and interview.
notes: Pay rates come from the 2026 city flyer and may change. The flyer says you must register in person to get the class fee discount. Fees are waived for current city employees.
duration: Year-round and seasonal jobs
pay_detail: Lifeguard $15 an hour. Lifeguard with water safety instructor $16. Assistant $14. Laborer $14. Pool manager $18. East side pools add 50 cents an hour.

who_can_apply: People 15 years and older. A swim skills test is part of the process.
how_to_apply: Use the link on the program page to apply online. Then do the swim test: 50 yards of freestyle, 50 yards of freestyle with a rescue tube, tread water 1 minute without hands, and pick up a 10 pound object from the bottom.
notes: The county notice has no date, so check that hiring is still open. Phone: (702) 455-1708. County pools are different from City of Las Vegas pools.
duration: Seasonal pools are open to the public May to August. Other hours and dates are not stated on the program page.
pay_detail: Pay rate is not stated on the program page. Lifeguard training is paid.

who_can_apply: Boys and girls ages 13 to 17. You cannot have a history of discipline problems in Clark County programs. You cannot have been suspended or expelled from school this school year, or last school year if you apply for a summer spot.
how_to_apply: Fill out, sign and turn in two forms. They are the Teen Leader application and a Clark County Volunteer application. Then you have an interview with the Leader of the Future supervisor at your center. Contact your local center for details.
notes: Centers include Desert Breeze, Cambridge, Helen Meyer and Hollywood. Others are Moapa Valley, Paradise, Parkdale and Bob Price. Also on the list are Silverado Ranch, Walnut and Whitney. The last two are Pearson and Winchester Dondero. You are picked from the written application, the interview and open spots.
duration: New teen leaders can volunteer up to 15 hours a week in the school year and up to 20 hours a week during vacations.
pay_detail: Volunteer position.

who_can_apply: Students age 16 or older in a Nevada high school or homeschool program, with a 2.5 GPA on a 4.0 scale. Some partner schools let students in grades 9 to 12 enroll. CSN may make exceptions.
how_to_apply: Fill out the CSN Admissions Application for High School and Early College Programs. You get an NSHE ID in 3 to 5 days. Then send placement scores for English or math, go to the online orientation, and sign up for classes.
notes: Classes are at the Charleston, Henderson and North Las Vegas campuses, at several centers, or online. Discount rates do not apply in summer. CSN also lists a CTE College Credit program. It gives free college credit for some high school career classes.
duration: By semester
pay_detail: For 2026 to 2027: $92.00 per credit plus an $11.50 per credit technology fee, plus any special course fees. No application fee. Check with your high school about payment.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12 at a high school that works with CSN on Jumpstart. You need a 2.5 GPA on a 4.0 scale. CSN may make exceptions with your school district.
how_to_apply: Fill out the CSN Admissions Application for High School and Early College Programs. There is no application fee. CSN emails you an NSHE ID. English and math classes also need a placement test or ACT or SAT scores.
notes: Partners include Clark County School District, charter schools and private schools in the Las Vegas area. Ask your counselor which Jumpstart classes your school offers.
duration: One course at a time, during the school year
pay_detail: $110 per course for the 2026 to 2027 school year, paid to your high school. Textbooks are free from your high school.

who_can_apply: Students in the ninth grade and above can join as Junior Members.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now button on the program page. It links to jmprogram@cyberclinicofficial.org. Questions go to the same email.
notes: UNLV Early Outreach lists this program for high school students with weekly online workshops at no cost. The program page itself does not state the schedule, so ask before you plan around it.
duration: Not stated on the program page. UNLV's youth page says weekly online workshops.
pay_detail: Cost and pay are not stated on the program page. UNLV's youth page lists it as no cost.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 14 to 17. No experience needed.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer form on the page. Watch for a confirmation email. Then go to a volunteer orientation, which is a must. Contact Volunteer@DiscoveryKidsLV.org or (702) 382-3445 ext. 110.
notes: The page does not say if a parent must sign. Teen volunteers are not presenters; you can apply for presenter roles at 18.
duration: Flexible schedule around school. Hours not stated.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Page mentions community service hours or work experience.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 15 to 17. You must have finished volunteer training in all 8 galleries and be an active volunteer in good standing.
how_to_apply: Meet the volunteer needs first. Then use the link on the page to the museum job page. Questions: volunteer@discoverykidslv.org or (702) 382-3445 ext. 110.
notes: You have to volunteer first, so start with the Teen Volunteer Program.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Page says paid but gives no rate

who_can_apply: Teens and young adults ages 16 to 24, in school or out of school. The page lists no other rules.
how_to_apply: Call 702.602.5199 or visit EmployNVYouthHub.org. The hub is at West Charleston Library, 6301 W. Charleston Blvd.
notes: Teens 16 and up only. The next-door Teen Zone is a separate space for ages 12 to 18.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Services are free. Paid training and internships are offered; pay not stated.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 18. You need to read basic English and follow instructions.
how_to_apply: The page has a Volunteer portal link (app.betterimpact.com). You can also call (702) 734-READ (7323). It does not describe the steps.
notes: The page does not say if a parent signature is needed. Ask the library.
duration: 4 to 12 hours per week for 4 weeks
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Age 16 or older. Ages 14 to 15 can volunteer with a parent or guardian. Students needing service hours can use the student sign-up.
how_to_apply: Students use the Student Volunteer Sign Up at lvnhm.org/community-service-hours-request. Others use lvnhm.org/volunteer-application. Finish safety training. Call (702) 384-3466 for the steps for parent permission.
notes: The page does not describe the permission form for 14 and 15 year olds, so call first.
duration: At least 4 hours per month
pay_detail: Unpaid. Students can earn community service hours.

who_can_apply: Anyone 14 or older. Ages 14 to 17 must turn in a parental permission agreement.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form with the Apply Now link on the page. Ages 14 to 17 also send in the parent permission form.
notes: Page does not mention training or required hours.
duration: Not stated. They want long-term volunteers; group projects can be one day or an afternoon.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Can count for community service hours.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 15 to 17 who like health care careers. Only 25 are accepted.
how_to_apply: Use the Medical Explorer Application link on the volunteer page. It works only in the open window. Then you have an interview in person. To get in you need a background check, a drug test, a shot check and a TB blood test.
notes: Process can take 4 to 6 weeks. The summer 2026 window was March 2 to April 3, so check the page for the next summer window. Adults 18 and over use a different application.
duration: 12 volunteer hours a month in the school year, 8 hours a week in summer. Must attend 75 percent of post activities.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program

who_can_apply: Ages 10 and up. Kids 10 to 15 must have a parent or guardian with them the whole time. Teens 16 and 17 may come alone with a signed waiver.
how_to_apply: Fill out the individual application to make an account. Then pick a session on the volunteer calendar. Ages 16 and 17 bring a signed waiver to every session.
notes: Wear closed toe shoes and knee length shorts or pants. Groups should book 4 to 8 weeks ahead. Volunteer office: 702-644-3663 ext. 349.
duration: Sessions you book on the volunteer calendar
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Current high school students with a 3.0 or higher cumulative GPA. Juniors and seniors get preference.
how_to_apply: Fill out the interest form linked on the page. If you have questions, send an email to hospitalityadmissions@unlv.edu.
notes: The page says both a 3.0 GPA rule and that any current high school student can attend. Ask the college which applies.
duration: Monday June 21 to Friday June 25, 2027
pay_detail: $850, includes meals and on-campus housing. Scholarships available: email kaila.seidler@unlv.edu.

who_can_apply: Most camps took students entering grades 9 to 12 or 10 to 12, plus 2026 high school graduates. The archaeology camp took students entering grades 8 to 10.
how_to_apply: Each camp has its own online registration form, listed in the news article. For prices, email Mary Rose Stark at maryrose.stark@unlv.edu.
notes: This is a 2026 news article. Check UNLV for the next summer list. The 2026 camp dates were Mock Trial June 1 to 5, Witnessing History June 8 to 12, Justice Law and Society June 15 to 17, Pathways to Success June 22 to 26, and Archaeology July 6 to 8.
duration: Each 2026 camp ran 3 to 5 days.
pay_detail: Cost varies by camp. The cost is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Rising 9th to 12th graders and select rising 8th graders from any high school. Outreach to Title I schools and students from groups with fewer opportunities.
how_to_apply: Use the Get More Info link on the page for the online form. Questions: 702-895-3375 or coe.yccr@unlv.edu.
notes: Page still shows the 2026 cycle. Expect applications to open around December again, and confirm with UNLV.
duration: Not stated on the page
pay_detail: $110 registration and enrollment fee. Scholarships available for students with financial need.

who_can_apply: Open to all high school students in Southern Nevada. Students outside the area can join the live online option.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online application. Then send the Parent Agreement Form by the due date, by email to sistem@unlv.edu or by mail. If you are accepted you get a registration link, a health form and a liability form.
notes: The program page does not list the session dates. A parent must sign the Parent Agreement Form. Students outside Southern Nevada can join the live virtual session.
duration: 5 sessions. You must attend all 5 to get a certificate.
pay_detail: Free. The program page says there is no fee. It does not pay students.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 18 and enrolled in high school. You need a grade point average of 2.5 or higher, good English, and the ability to do tasks on your own.
how_to_apply: Download the teen application from the program page. Fill it out with a parent consent form, a school records release, and a teacher or counselor evaluation. After review you get an interview. Call the volunteer office at the hospital you want.
notes: The application lists these hospitals: Centennial Hills, Valley, Henderson, Summerlin, Spring Valley and West Henderson. You also need a health screening. That includes a TB skin test each year. You must go to an orientation. Summerlin Hospital volunteer office phone: 702-233-7532.
duration: Minimum 75 hours a year. The number varies by hospital.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role. You must buy a volunteer shirt.

who_can_apply: New Mexico youth ages 14 to 25. The page says jobs are open to this age range in general.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. Get 2 character reference forms from people who are not family. Then interview. Paper forms can be turned in at the YMCA or the Los Alamos or Espanola Teen Centers. Questions: lzollinger@laymca.org.
notes: The page says the 2026 grant award status was pending. The page does not state a wage.
duration: 2026: crew members June 1 to July 24
pay_detail: Paid jobs. Wage not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: In school: ages 14 to 21 and low income. You also need one more need. Examples are foster care, homelessness, a disability, or being an English learner. Out of school: ages 16 to 24 with a need listed on the program page.
how_to_apply: Check that you qualify. Gather a photo ID that shows your date of birth and your Social Security card. Create an Arizona Job Connection PLUS account. Visit the client portal first. Career centers are in Mesa, Glendale, Surprise and Tempe.
notes: Not every teen qualifies. You must meet the age and need rules. Services are free. Pay for work experience is not stated on the program page.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Services are free. Some youth get paid work experience. The program page does not give the pay rate.

who_can_apply: High school students. The page does not list exact ages or a city rule.
how_to_apply: Apply through the MCA Denver teens page when the window opens.
notes: Meets Wednesdays 4:30 to 6:30 PM all school year. Admission to MCA Denver is free for teens. Exact 2026 to 2027 dates are not posted, so this uses the usual pattern.
duration: Meets Wednesdays 4:30 to 6:30 PM all school year
pay_detail: Up to $300 per semester.

who_can_apply: High school students. The page does not list exact ages or a city rule.
how_to_apply: Apply through the MCA Denver teens page when the window opens. Email teens@mcadenver.org with questions.
notes: Meets Tuesdays 4:30 to 6:30 PM, one semester. Admission to MCA Denver is free for teens. Exact 2026 to 2027 dates are not posted, so this uses the usual pattern.
duration: Meets Tuesdays 4:30 to 6:30 PM, one semester
pay_detail: Up to $300 for the semester.

who_can_apply: Local teens interested in the arts. The page does not list exact ages or grades.
how_to_apply: Apply through MCA Denver. How to apply is not stated on the page; see the teens page.
notes: The stipend covers materials, not wages. The studio is open to the public.
duration: 3 to 4 weeks; studio open Tuesday to Friday, noon to 5 PM
pay_detail: The museum gives a stipend for materials. A personal pay amount is not stated.

who_can_apply: Ages 13 to 15.
how_to_apply: The page gives no steps. Contact Mesa Aquatics at 480-644-7529 or aquatics@mesaaz.gov.
notes: Part of the City of Mesa H.Y.P.E. Teen Programs page.
duration: Summer. Exact dates not listed.
pay_detail: Volunteer role. The page says it leads to future lifeguarding.

who_can_apply: Teens can use the Teen Application. The page does not state the age range. Call to ask.
how_to_apply: Apply and interview. Then a health screen and background check. Then orientation. Use the Teen Application or Summer Student Application on the page, or call (480) 412-3258.
notes: Teen age range is not stated on the page. Banner Desert Medical Center is in Mesa.
duration: At least 6 months or 100 hours
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Volunteer Application on the page or call (480) 321-4122. The process includes an interview and background research and can take up to 3 weeks.
notes: The Banner volunteer pages are not the same for each hospital. Call first, then apply.
duration: At least 100 hours within 6 months, or one shift of about 4 hours per week
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 18, and you must be in school. Keep a C average. You need medical clearance before starting.
how_to_apply: Sign up during the August window on the program page. For questions, contact Program Coordinator Christine Mendoza. The page shows 480-644-5047 and 480-644-3883, so confirm before calling.
notes: The work is hard on the body. Cadets lift, pull or push up to 75 lbs. Community service is strongly encouraged but not required.
duration: Not stated on the program page. Most meetings are held at the Public Safety Training Facility, 3260 North 40th Street, Mesa.
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17. You must be 13 by the start of the program. Space is limited.
how_to_apply: Sign up for a camp in ActiveNet. Then get a form and an interview link. Then do the interview and the training you must take. Adaptive camps (Camp Fiesta, Wiggles & Giggles) need a form and interview before you sign up.
notes: The City of Mesa website blocked a normal page visit, so the facts come from the 2026 FAQ PDF. Check the Mesa summer registration dates. Contact: PRCFVolunteers@mesaaz.gov or 480-644-4345 (from a search listing, not the PDF).
duration: Summer camp season. Mandatory training dates differ by camp.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Program fee is $32 for Mesa residents and $38 for non-residents.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 19, and you must have finished 8th grade. Stay in school until you graduate. Keep a 2.0 GPA or higher. No serious police record.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online interest form on the Mesa cadet page. A cadet advisor then contacts you. For help, call 480-644-4869 or email PDCadets@mesaaz.gov.
notes: Members can stay in the Post until they turn 21. Cadets also do community service. Ask the post for the next recruiting date.
duration: Weekly meetings on Thursday nights
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the program page. No fee is listed.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 13 to 18 (high school students) in Nevada 4-H.
how_to_apply: Email nevada4h@unr.edu with questions. The page does not say how to sign up for Capital Days.
notes: Activities also include a visit to the state museum and the Governor's Mansion. Ask Nevada 4-H for dates and cost.
duration: Trip dates not posted
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Members are ages 9 to 19 as of January 1 of the current year. Younger Cloverbuds are ages 5 to 8.
how_to_apply: Contact your county Extension office to enroll and find a club.
notes: Also open to younger kids. Fee amounts are set by each county and club. Ask your county Extension office.
duration: Ongoing
pay_detail: Costs vary: project books, project supplies, a county activity fee, club dues and event fees.

who_can_apply: High school or homeschool students in good behavior and academic standing with a GPA of 2.5 or higher. Your high school must approve. Talk to your counselor before you sign up.
how_to_apply: Fill out the WNC application if you are new to WNC. Check your email for your NSHE ID and your WNC login. Send the high school authorization form with a student and parent signature. Then sign up for classes in myWNC. Questions: 775-445-3277.
notes: The page mentions a Fallon campus and Fernley offerings. After you pass a class, you must ask WNC to send your transcript to your high school. Allow up to five business days for WNC to process your school's approval.
duration: By semester
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the dual credit page. WNC lists fees on a separate page.

who_can_apply: Nevada students in 8th, 9th or 10th grade, so you can finish the two year term in high school. You apply for the Senate district where you live or go to school.
how_to_apply: Fill out and sign the application, which has short essays. Add one letter of recommendation. Send it by email, fax or mail. Questions: info@youthleg.state.nv.us or (775) 684-6740.
notes: Each of the 21 state senators appoints one Youth Legislator. Meetings are often on weekday afternoons and may mean missing class. The brochure is the 2024 edition, so confirm the grade rule and dates with the program.
duration: Two year term, June 1 to May 31. Eleven required meetings and trainings.
pay_detail: Unpaid. The program pays for the one day and two day trainings, including travel, meals and lodging.

who_can_apply: Any New Mexico youth ages 5 to 18 can join. You do not need a farm or any skills. Cloverbuds are ages 5 to 8. Novice is 9 to 11. Junior is 12 to 13. Senior is 14 to 18.
how_to_apply: Contact your County Extension Office and talk with your 4-H agent. Then create a family account and enroll at 4h.zsuite.org. Returning members re-enroll each year, update projects and submit the required forms.
notes: State office phone on the page is 575-646-3026. Call it if you are not sure which county you are in.
duration: Ongoing
pay_detail: New Mexico 4-H generally has no statewide membership fee. Some counties, clubs or projects have costs for supplies, livestock, workshops or camps. Ask your County Extension Office.

who_can_apply: Students in New Mexico ag education programs. The association says it serves over 5,300 members in over 85 schools. No age or grade rule is stated.
how_to_apply: The site lists FFA chapter lists, a 2026-2027 plan for events, scholarships and Jr. High contests.
notes: Some pages on this site carry a 2022 copyright, so camp fees and dates may be out of date. Confirm with your ag teacher or the state office. The homepage does not show the $225 camp fee, so confirm it before relying on it.
duration: School year. Leadership Camp is a separate event.
pay_detail: Leadership Camp fee was $225 per camper on a page that looks older (copyright 2022). Camp scholarships were offered.

who_can_apply: Young people from forest-dependent communities in New Mexico. The summer program is for high school age youth. The Guild says its work covers ages 16 to 25.
how_to_apply: Watch the Guild's FSYC page for position descriptions and application forms. Crew member information is posted on the project page later in the year.
notes: The New Mexico Youth Conservation Corps Commission and the Cibola and Santa Fe National Forests pay for part of it. Past crew members who log 640 hours may get a federal hiring status. Pay and crew sites could not be read on the pages checked.
duration: Early June to early August (2026)
pay_detail: Paid. The hourly rate is not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Ages 17 to 30, per the 2027 job list. No earlier experience is needed for crew member jobs.
how_to_apply: Open the apply page and find the 2027 Conservation Crew Corpsmember job in Albuquerque or Taos. Then use its Apply Now link.
notes: The work is outdoors. The program page says ages 17 to 25, and the job list says 17 to 30. Ask RMYC if you are close to the top age. Some crews camp for 8 days in a row, then have 6 days off. Corpsmembers who complete a full AmeriCorps season become eligible for a scholarship award. The FAQ lists UNM College Credit as a member benefit.
duration: Seasonal, full time (40 or more hours a week). The end date is not stated on the program page.
pay_detail: $700 per week for the 2027 Corpsmember job. Paid by stipend.

who_can_apply: You must be ages 16 to 24. You live in Bernalillo, Sandoval, Valencia or Torrance County. The page lists no other rules.
how_to_apply: Call 505-818-1428 (WIOA Youth inquiries) or 505-977-3216, or use the contact form on the program page.
notes: Ask YDI if you qualify.
duration: Year-round
pay_detail: Work experience is part of the program. Wage not stated.

who_can_apply: You must be ages 14 to 24. You live in Cibola, Colfax, Los Alamos, McKinley, Mora, Rio Arriba, San Juan, San Miguel, Santa Fe or Taos County. The page lists no other rules.
how_to_apply: Contact YDI through the form on the program page or call 505-977-3216 (Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m.).
notes: WIOA programs have federal rules on who qualifies. Ask YDI if you qualify.
duration: Year-round support. Paid work experience typically runs 250 to 350 hours.
pay_detail: Paid work experience. Wage not stated.

who_can_apply: New Mexico youth ages 14 to 25. Local governments, tribes and nonprofits apply for state funding and then hire the corps members.
how_to_apply: Find a funded project near you on the YCC projects map. Then contact that sponsor about jobs. A sponsor can be a city, county, tribe or nonprofit.
notes: Teens do not apply to the state. The state funds sponsors, who do the hiring. Pay, dates and application steps vary by sponsor. The projects map on this page shows 2021 to 2023 projects, and older ones are on a separate Projects page.
duration: Set by each sponsor
pay_detail: Pay not stated on this page. Returning corps members can earn a $500 cash benefit or a $1,500 education voucher.

who_can_apply: Teens. The page does not list ages or grades.
how_to_apply: Join the email list on the page to hear when applications open.
notes: The first group of Fellows began in fall 2023.
duration: A yearly group (the 2026 to 2027 group is already chosen)
pay_detail: Described as a paid internship. The pay rate is not stated.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 14 to 18 who can attend all required group meetings.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the next application opens. Email Erin Shupe or call 801-581-3774 with questions. Subscribe to quarterly updates on the page.
notes: Meetings are Wednesdays 6 to 8 PM, plus some Saturdays. Later you work 2 gallery shifts of 2.5 hours a month.
duration: School year group: October 7, 2026 to April 14, 2027, about 90 hours. A summer group runs June to August.
pay_detail: Hourly wage starting at $13.00. You can choose to volunteer instead. Staff can ride UTA transit free during the internship.

who_can_apply: High school students who live in Ogden City.
how_to_apply: Fill out the form at the bottom of the program page. Questions go to the Council Communications Director at 801-629-8103.
notes: This is a competitive process. Only the top rated applicants take part.
duration: The council meets 1 to 2 times each month.
pay_detail: No pay.

who_can_apply: High school juniors and seniors.
how_to_apply: First pay online and write down your confirmation number. Then fill out the application form linked on the program page. Print all documents before check in.
notes: The 2026 page listed 35 seats. Use the email on the program page for questions.
duration: 4 days (July 13 to 16 in 2026)
pay_detail: $350. This covers a t-shirt, lodging, meals and lab supplies.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 18. Graduating seniors can apply.
how_to_apply: Apply online. Campers are picked in early May based on interest in business and a desire to learn. You can fill out the interest form to get an email when applications open.
notes: The page mentions dorm life for campers. The camp is hosted with the Utah Association of Certified Public Accountants.
duration: 4 days and 3 nights (June 8 to 11 in 2026)
pay_detail: No pay. The camp is free because of community sponsors.

who_can_apply: Utah high school students in grades 9 to 11. The page says it is especially for first-generation college learners.
how_to_apply: Apply online. Share your interests, your goals and why you want to join. The application asks for short written responses, which carry strong weight. The team picks students by readiness, interest and fit. Applications can also go on the waitlist.
notes: You must go in person. Classes also have homework outside class time. Track choice is not guaranteed. Questions: text 801-928-7615. The page says you may be added to a contact list for future openings.
duration: 7 weeks. Tuesdays to Thursdays, 9:00 AM to 3:15 PM (June 24 to Aug 7 in 2026)
pay_detail: No pay. Tuition is free for admitted students. You pay for your own rides, lunches and personal costs.

who_can_apply: Anyone 15 or older. It is picky, so not all applicants are accepted.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer form linked on the page. Do a phone interview. Then go to a volunteer orientation. Volunteer Manager: 602.716.2037.
notes: The Teens page also lists a Teen Advisory Board, but gives no ages or dates. Email teenadvisory@azscience.org to ask.
duration: At least 24 hours of service. Weekly shifts, event help, days, evenings or weekends.
pay_detail: Unpaid. May earn service-learning credit.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 21. Must be legally able to work in the U.S. A background check may be required. The page does not say whether Club membership is required; its application asks whether you are a BGCAZ member.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form (10 to 15 minutes). Then go to a Zoom info session and interview with staff. Then do the AZYF Academy at hubs in Mesa and Glendale. Apply at azyouthforce.org/apply.
notes: You may face a background check and a pre-employment drug test. Pay, length and exact dates were not on the pages, so email Samantha.Hansen@bgcaz.org or Kevin.Chavez@bgcaz.org.
duration: 30-hour academy first, then the internship. Length not stated on the program pages.
pay_detail: Paid internship. Rate not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17.
how_to_apply: Use the Sign Up link on the volunteer page. Fill out the online volunteer form.
notes: The page does not give a schedule or minimum hours. Ask the volunteer office.
duration: Short-term, seasonal or ongoing, depending on the role
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 21. The page lists no other rules.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Here link on the program page to be told when applications open. Questions: youthservices@gphxul.org.
notes: The page still talks about the 2026 application, so it may be out of date. Call or email to confirm the next cycle.
duration: 5 weeks, 110 paid hours
pay_detail: Paid for 110 hours of work and job readiness workshops. Hourly rate not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 9 to 12 during the school year, at least 13 at the start of the school year.
how_to_apply: Apply online when it opens in mid-May 2027. The page does not give steps. Contact studentvolunteers@honorhealth.com.
notes: Medical Explorers meet at Thompson Peak, Deer Valley and John C. Lincoln Medical Centers. The Nursing Explorers meet near Deer Valley Medical Center.
duration: Monthly meetings
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: High school and college students 16 and older. Parent or guardian consent is needed under 18.
how_to_apply: Send in the Student form on the page. Meet the volunteer team. Pass a background check and drug test. Then finish orientation and training. Call 480.245.6915 or email volunteer@MIM.org.
notes: Museum is at 4725 E. Mayo Blvd., Phoenix. The background check and drug test are required.
duration: Summer: one full month, at least 2 shifts a week. Year-round: at least 2 shifts a month.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Student volunteers do not need a museum membership.

who_can_apply: Age 15 or older for these roles. Lifeguards need a lifeguard certificate first (StarGuard Elite or the city class).
how_to_apply: Get lifeguard certified (class cost for a short time: $40) or use an active StarGuard Elite card. Then apply online. Search "Aquatics" in the City of Phoenix job portal. Questions: 602-534-6587 or aquatics.pks@phoenix.gov.
notes: Swim Lesson Instructors also need a Starfish Swim Instructor certificate. A certificate or an application does not promise a job. The page does not name a work permit rule.
duration: Season dates not listed on the page
pay_detail: Lifeguard $17.72/hr, Shallow Water Lifeguard $16.88, Swim Lesson Instructor $19.54, Pool Cashier and Buddy Bear $15.69.

who_can_apply: Age 14 and older, and you must have finished 8th grade. Stay in school until you graduate. Keep at least a C average. No serious police record.
how_to_apply: Complete the Cadet Application Packet and bring it to testing night. Use the APPLY NOW link on the page. For recruitment, call 602-534-2677.
notes: New cadets serve a three-month probation. During that time they must do 8 hours of community service each month. At 18, cadets can apply for non-sworn positions, such as Police Assistants.
duration: Weekly meetings every Tuesday at 5:00 PM
pay_detail: Unpaid. Cadets are volunteers, not police employees.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17.
how_to_apply: Follow the steps on phoenixpubliclibrary.org/teens/summer-teen-volunteers. Then staff contact you for an interview. Turn in a signed Volunteer PHX Permission Form and waiver by your first day.
notes: Based on the 2026 cycle. Expect applications again in spring 2027. Four online orientations were offered in May.
duration: At least 4 weeks over the summer, plus one online orientation and branch training
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 24 when you apply. You live in the City of Phoenix. You have papers that show you can legally work in the U.S.
how_to_apply: The page does not describe the steps or give an apply link. Watch the City of Phoenix internships page for the next session. Selection was first come, first served.
notes: Only Phoenix residents. You must be able to work the whole program. Teens must be 16 or older. The page does not say whether a work permit is needed.
duration: 4 weeks, 20 hours per week, 80 hours total (June to July 2026 session)
pay_detail: $15.15 per hour (2026 session)

who_can_apply: High school students ages 14 to 17.
how_to_apply: Apply with the online form the museum shares. Go to orientation and teen front desk training. Shadow a front desk volunteer for at least 4 shifts before working on your own.
notes: Teen Leaders help train new teen volunteers and help develop new program materials. Ask the museum for the current application form.
duration: Saturday mornings or afternoons, October to April. Minimum 3 to 4 hours a month.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Free museum entry and a store discount. The page says it counts for volunteer and internship graduation hours.

who_can_apply: Age 12 and older with an adult. Age 16 and older can volunteer without an adult.
how_to_apply: Go to the volunteer portal on the food bank site. Make a login and pick a shift by site and activity.
notes: Teens 12 to 15 must come with an adult. Court-ordered volunteers should call 602-343-3135.
duration: Usually 2 to 3 hours at the Phoenix and Surprise sites. Food box packing shifts are 2 hours. Mobile distribution shifts run 3 to 5 hours.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 9 to 12. You do not need volunteer experience.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. If chosen, you get an interview. Then you get a yes or no. Join the interest list on the page. Questions: zooteens@phoenixzoo.org.
notes: Orientation and training are a must in August and September. Trailblazers Youth Advisory Council is a leadership choice. You can apply to both. You can join only 1.
duration: August to May, one 5-hour weekend shift per month
pay_detail: Unpaid. Teens get a Teen Volunteer membership after two of eight monthly shifts.

who_can_apply: Applications are open to people 13 and older. If you are 13 to 17 you need a parent or guardian permission.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the library volunteer system. If you do not want to apply online, email Karen Goates at kgoates@ppld.org.
notes: The age range 13 to 17 comes from the rule that people 13 and older apply and teens under 18 need permission. Call (719) 531-6333, ext. 6146 with questions.
duration: Summer Adventure season (2026). Other teen roles vary.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: High school students entering grades 9 to 12 who are ages 14 to 17. You must be 14 before your first shift.
how_to_apply: Check the page in spring for the application link. Email volunteer@redbutte.utah.edu.
notes: Garden work can mean kneeling, weeding and standing on uneven ground.
duration: Dates not announced
pay_detail: Volunteer and intern roles. Pay is not stated.

who_can_apply: Ages 11 to 14 by the first session date. You must pass a swim test: 25 yards of front crawl, a step into deep water with a 10 foot underwater swim, and 1 minute of treading water.
