how_to_apply: Pick a session on the program page. Each session links to a registration page, and the site has an Online Registration link. For questions, call Parks Administration at 775-334-2262.
notes: This is a good step toward the City of Reno lifeguard class, which starts at age 15. You must attend every day of a session to be certified.
duration: 4 days, 8:30am to 1:30pm each day
pay_detail: The class fee is $100.

who_can_apply: You must be 15 by the final scheduled session. You must also pass a swim test. Swim 150 yards, then tread water for 2 minutes using only your legs. Swim 50 yards. Then finish a timed event in 1 minute 40 seconds: a 20 yard swim, a dive to 10 feet for a 10 pound object, a swim back, and an exit without a ladder.
how_to_apply: Use the Register Online button for a class, or join the interest list by email. To get the free certificate, apply online for a city job. Be onboarded by the class start date.
notes: You must attend every day of the class to be certified. A shorter $124 renewal class is for people with a valid lifeguard certificate, or one that ended in the last 30 days. The program page does not say if a work permit is needed.
duration: In-person class days run 9am to 3:30pm. The class is blended, with online lecture and in-class training.
pay_detail: The class costs $140. The page says the city will certify you for free if you are hired and onboarded by the class start date.

who_can_apply: Under 16 can do drop-in single-day tasks with a parent-signed release form. 16 and older can do continuous volunteering after a background check. No minimum age is stated.
how_to_apply: Drop in: a parent signs the Volunteer Release of Liability Form and you sign a time sheet. Ongoing: send in a Volunteer Application, a Consent and Disclosure form and a Reno PD background form. Get a photo ID card. Call the Volunteer Coordinator at 775-334-2046.
notes: The listed roles on the page are mostly for seniors programs and fund raising. Ask the coordinator what fits a teen.
duration: Drop-in single days, or recurring scheduled tasks
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Open to grades 8 to 12.
how_to_apply: Use the Teen Assistant Application button on the page (online form). Then a 15-minute Zoom interview and an in-person training. Contact Kristen Kellogg, 775-398-5920, kkellogg@nvdm.org.
notes: You must be free during Washoe County School District breaks.
duration: Camp breaks: fall, winter, spring and summer (Washoe County School District breaks)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role. Earns over 80 community service hours.

who_can_apply: Bilingual English and Spanish high school juniors in Northern Nevada. Up to 30 are chosen for the summer program.
how_to_apply: Fill out the CBESS Interest Form at nevada.formstack.com/forms/cbess. Questions: cbess@unr.edu or (775) 784-1110.
notes: Chosen students also do an outreach internship. Up to 64 more juniors get a certificate. They must first finish some questionnaires.
duration: One week on campus plus two or more weeks virtual, then monthly mentoring in senior year
pay_detail: Free to attend. A stipend is not mentioned.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17.
how_to_apply: Sign up online when it opens on February 1. For a scholarship, add an essay on your interests and a teacher recommendation letter to the form. Questions: paigefroese@unr.edu.
notes: Camp prices and dates were not posted when this was checked. Check back before February.
duration: Camp dates not listed on the page
pay_detail: Fee not listed on the page. A $50 non-refundable deposit can hold a spot; full payment is due within a month of registering. Scholarships available.

who_can_apply: Nevada high school students who meet each course's prerequisites. A counselor or vice principal must back you. That lets the classes count toward graduation.
how_to_apply: Fill out the UNR non-degree student application and the dual enrollment interest form. Send your shot records through the online portal (2 MMR doses and 1 Tdap). Upload your high school transcripts with the Transcript Upload form. Your counselor or vice principal fills out the school district contract form. They email it to DualEnrollment@unr.edu.
notes: Earlier college work can place you into classes. So can SAT or ACT scores, AP or IB scores, or placement tests.
duration: By semester
pay_detail: $154 per credit for tuition plus an $18 per credit tech fee, plus any class fees.

who_can_apply: Nevada high school juniors and seniors. The program is aimed most at girls and young women who have faced barriers to STEM learning and research.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply now link on the Join Women in STEM page. A paper form can be picked up at the Dean's Office, 4th floor of the Davidson Mathematics and Science Center on campus.
notes: The program page still shows the 2024 to 2025 year. Check with the program before you plan on it. It asks for four events in each of three event series, two advisor meetings and three mentor meetings during the year.
duration: One school year
pay_detail: Cost and pay are not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18. Teen and a parent or guardian both sign the application.
how_to_apply: Online: make a Beanstack account and join the Volunteen Challenge. A coordinator emails the forms. Paper: fill out the online form or ask the volunteer coordinator at your branch.
notes: Paperwork and orientation come first. Both a teen and a parent or guardian must sign.
duration: Self-paced, up to 20 hours
pay_detail: Unpaid. You get a certificate at 20 hours.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 6 to 12 in Northwest Colorado. Groups: Adventurers (6th and 7th), Trailblazers (8th and 9th), Outdoor Leaders (10th to 12th).
how_to_apply: Contact the Youth Programs team: Kimberly Tholis (Director) or Shawn O'Kane (Manager). The page has a Reach Out link.
notes: More than 200 teens join each year. Based in Steamboat Springs. Parents have a policy page.
duration: Two or four weeks
pay_detail: The page does not state pay. The Colorado Youth Corps Association lists the youth program as ages 14 to 18, so ask whether your group is paid.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 7 to 12.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now button on the library teens page.
notes: The apply page (services.slcpl.org/teensquad) did not load in our reader, so the dates of each six week session are not confirmed. Ask the library when the next session starts.
duration: Six weeks
pay_detail: Volunteer hours. No pay stated.

who_can_apply: Rising high school seniors. The current page says students graduating in 2028 can apply. Younger students are removed. The page lists no age rule. Freshmen through juniors can use a separate boot camp.
how_to_apply: Send an application with a teacher recommendation, an essay and transcripts. Transcripts must list every high school course and grade. An interview may follow.
notes: Students must attend orientation, cohort meetings and the poster event. Housing is not provided, though the page mentions a University Guest House on campus where interns are not supervised. The page says there is no cost to join. It does not say whether interns are paid. The page does not say which year the June 8 to July 31 dates belong to.
duration: 8 weeks, June 8 to July 31, 30 hours a week (9 a.m. to 3 p.m., Monday to Friday)
pay_detail: Unpaid. It costs nothing to join. Housing is not provided.

who_can_apply: High school students ready to start Calculus. You do not need to have taken it. Students between junior and senior year are preferred. Costs are paid for US citizens, nationals and permanent residents.
how_to_apply: Email four items to the program contact on the program page: an application form, a personal statement, a recommendation form and your school transcripts. All four are needed. Picks are based on merit.
notes: This is not a live-in program. Students who live far away must arrange their own housing. You must be able to attend the whole program. The 2026 program was in person.
duration: June 16 to July 2 in 2026, Monday to Friday, 10 a.m. to 4 p.m.
pay_detail: Free in 2026 for US citizens, nationals and permanent residents. You earn 3 college credits (credit or no credit).

who_can_apply: Ages 12 and up. If you are under 18 and sign up on your own, an adult must come with you. High school youth groups can sign up too, with one adult leader for every six youth.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer request form. Pick the Salt Lake Main location, your group type and the shifts you want. Families with kids 6 to 11 use separate family shifts.
notes: The form also lists other sites in St. George, Springville and Blanding. Some fundraiser jobs, like hanging race posters, are for ages 16 and up. Shift times on the form include weekday days, weekday evenings and Saturday mornings.
duration: Warehouse shifts are 90 minutes
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer work.

who_can_apply: Salt Lake City youth. The morning sessions are open to grades 7 to 12. The afternoon sessions are open to grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: The pages do not describe how to apply. Contact Erica Andino at (385) 309-7439.
notes: The Salt Lake City site blocked our regular reader, so this was read through a page summary tool. The two pages disagree about grades, so check before you apply.
duration: 6 weeks, Monday to Friday, mornings (Child Development I) or afternoons (II)
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Salt Lake City high school students. Summer interns are grades 9 to 12.
how_to_apply: The pages do not describe how to apply. Contact Angela Romero or Lucy Leishman at 385-299-5647.
notes: The Salt Lake City site would not load in a regular reader, so this came from a page summary. The teen page said applications were open until May 25. It also said no longer accepting. Confirm with the contact.
duration: School year: two groups meet Tuesdays and Thursdays, September 29, 2026 to April 29, 2027. Summer 2026: six weeks (Policy in Action Thursdays, Service Squad Tuesdays).
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Teens ages 16 to 18 who are work eligible.
how_to_apply: The program page gives no steps to apply. Call Erica Andino at (385) 309-7439. She is the Senior Community Programs Manager.
notes: This is the paid internship. The two unpaid Child Development internships on the same page (grades 7 to 12) are a different program. The school-year afterschool program on the page said it was no longer taking applications.
duration: 8 weeks. No start or end dates are posted.
pay_detail: Paid. The wage is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 12 to 18, based on a 2024 Teen Advisory Board listing. Ask your branch to confirm.
how_to_apply: Call or visit your neighborhood branch and ask about teen volunteering. The customer service number is 801-943-4636.
notes: The teen ages come from 2024 branch event listings. A 2024 summer teen event listed ages 14 to 17 and required attendance at one of three trainings. The main volunteer page does not name ages for teens. Volunteers over 18 must pass a background check.
duration: Teen Advisory Board meetings were listed for the first Thursday of the month in 2024.
pay_detail: Unpaid. Teens earn volunteer hours.

who_can_apply: Students in high school, career and trade programs. College and graduate students can apply too. The program page names no age limit.
how_to_apply: Search the county job board for posts with Internship as the position type. If none fits, call Human Resources at 385-468-0570. The program page says unpaid interns take part in an educational or academic program.
notes: Each job post says whether it is paid or for school credit. Read each post for its own rules.
duration: Varies. It depends on the office and its budget.
pay_detail: Some are paid and some are for school credit. Each job post says which.

who_can_apply: High school students. The page gives no residency or other rules.
how_to_apply: Not stated on the page. Contact SITE SANTA FE at info@sitesantafe.org or 505-989-1199.
notes: Ask about the start date and how to join.
duration: Ends with an exhibition (2026 show ran Feb 27 to Apr 4, 2026)
pay_detail: Free.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 16 to 24. The program serves young people from Northern New Mexico.
how_to_apply: Open the Youth Jobs Application link on the YouthWorks site. You can also email info@santafeyouthworks.org with your resume and letter of interest, or call 505-989-1855. The office is at 1505 Llano St., Santa Fe.
notes: The page also lists GED prep, First Aid and CPR training, and trades certificates.
duration: A 6 month spring and summer season, per the page. The season listed is for 2025.
pay_detail: Wages and stipends. The amount is not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: Teens must be at least 14 and not yet 18. A parent or guardian must give permission.
how_to_apply: Fill out the interest form on the program page. A teen volunteer coordinator will contact you. New summer volunteers must go to a required orientation.
notes: Space is limited, and applying does not guarantee a spot. The program page says the Mustang and Arabian school year programs are full. New summer volunteers must attend a general orientation.
duration: School year program runs September to May. Summer program runs June to July.
pay_detail: Unpaid. You earn documented volunteer hours.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 19 who live in the Scottsdale area.
how_to_apply: Call 480-312-0060 or email VistaCareerCenter@ScottsdaleAZ.gov to make an appointment. You can meet online or in person.
notes: The career center is at 7700 E. Roosevelt St., Scottsdale. It has a self-serve computer lab for job searches. The center is open Monday to Friday, 8 am to 5 pm. Specialists are available 8 am to 4 pm.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page. This program helps you find a job. It is not a job itself.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 17 who finished the Highwater Farm Summer Youth Program. You must commit to all 11 weeks.
how_to_apply: Start with the Summer Youth Program. Check the fall program page for details. Questions: savanna@highwaterfarm.org.
notes: Only for teens who completed the summer program.
duration: 11 weeks, Friday and Saturday (late August to early November)
pay_detail: Bi-weekly stipend (amount not stated), plus fresh produce on set days.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 17. You must be able to commit to the whole 7 weeks.
how_to_apply: The application will be on the program page in January 2027. Look for it then. Questions: savanna@highwaterfarm.org.
notes: Farm address: 7001 County Road 346, Silt, CO 81652. The 2027 pay rate is not posted. Page does not say which towns qualify.
duration: 7 weeks, Monday to Thursday, 8 AM to 3 PM (2026: June 15 to July 30)
pay_detail: $15.16 per hour (2026), plus job training and fresh produce on set days.

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 6 to 12. Grades 11 and 12 attend their own session.
how_to_apply: Fill out the registration form on the program page. Returning campers who did not get an early form should contact the team right away. If the camp is full, join the waiting list on the page.
notes: Campers stay in dorms with staff watching around the clock. The 2026 camp had 120 spots.
duration: One week. Grades 6 to 10: July 12 to 17, 2026. Grades 11 and 12: July 19 to 24, 2026.
pay_detail: No pay. The camp is free. Spots are first come, first served.

who_can_apply: Students entering sophomore, junior or senior year of high school. You need at least a 2.75 GPA and must have finished Algebra 1.
how_to_apply: The program page says application links are at the bottom of the page. The link itself is not stated on the program page.
notes: The page says you can earn college credit. The number of credits is not stated on the program page.
duration: One week per session
pay_detail: $675 per session. This covers food, housing and classes.

who_can_apply: High school students ages 14 to 18. You live in the Four Corners region. That is Archuleta, Dolores, La Plata, Montezuma and San Juan counties and northern New Mexico counties. Or you live in the Los Valles region. That is Park, Chaffee, Saguache, Mineral and Rio Grande, Alamosa, Costilla and Conejos counties.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply link for your region on the page. Find your region on the county map.
notes: The Colorado Youth Corps Association page lists other youth corps by county. They are Boulder County, Larimer County, Mile High Youth Corps and Rocky Mountain Youth Corps. The last has a youth program for ages 14 to 18 in Steamboat Springs. They also list Weld County and Western Colorado. Ask each one for the ages and dates.
duration: Two sessions: late May to June, or mid July to mid August. Each is 4 to 5 weeks.
pay_detail: $14.42 per hour, 32 to 40 hours per week

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 18. The job is in Taos, NM.
how_to_apply: Open the apply page and find the Youth Coalition Member job under Prevention Program. Use the link for that job.
notes: The job runs from Oct 9, 2026 to Apr 30, 2027, per the listing. Hours per week and the last day to apply are not stated on the program page. The Prevention Program listing says its positions are for people pursuing a career in public health addressing substance misuse.
pay_detail: $17 per hour

who_can_apply: Juniors and seniors at a Phoenix-area high school who can attend in person at the Tempe campus. Under 18 needs a parent or guardian sign-off.
how_to_apply: Application steps are not posted yet. Use the Contact CTF form on the page for updates.
notes: The page says it will be updated when the revamped program opens. Do not plan around it until dates are posted.
duration: About 8 weeks, mostly June and July, 15 to 20 hours per week
pay_detail: Not stated on the page

who_can_apply: Teens ages 13 to 17.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now button on the page.
notes: The volunteer page lists the program for events, summer camps and more.
duration: Not stated
pay_detail: Volunteer. Teens earn incentives. The page does not name them.

who_can_apply: High school girls. The page does not list grades. The program is accredited through Alpine School District for the fall and spring semesters only.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now button on the page. Questions: Stacie Wilding, swilding@thanksgivingpoint.org, 801-768-7426.
notes: The page says the credit is for fall and spring semesters only.
duration: 40 hours per semester for the district credit; some roles need more
pay_detail: Pay is not stated. Interns in some roles get a Thanksgiving Point Team Member Membership.

who_can_apply: Individual volunteers must be at least 15. Younger teens can volunteer with an adult. They fill out the Family Volunteer form.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Individual Volunteer form on the page.
notes: Group service projects for 5 to 25 people are also offered. Court ordered service is for 18 and older only.
duration: Ongoing
pay_detail: Unpaid. You get a free annual family membership after 20 volunteer hours.

who_can_apply: Teens 15 and older. A guardian enters their name to consent for a minor.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply now link on the volunteer page. You give contact info, free times, hours wanted, consent from a guardian and photo permission. Call (520) 792-9985 with questions.
notes: The museum hours listed on the page disagree, so confirm shift times.
duration: You choose hours on the application (daily, weekly, monthly or one time).
pay_detail: Unpaid. Can count for school service hours.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 17. Teens and parents must attend an orientation. Space is limited.
how_to_apply: Call Class Registration at 520-791-4877 or use the Register for Classes link on the page. Orientation details are emailed after you sign up. A Discount Program is there for people who need low income help.
notes: Aims at recreation careers. Contact 520-791-4873 for the schedule.
duration: Up to 30 hours per week. Program dates not listed.
pay_detail: Registration fee $25 for City residents, $30 for non-residents. The page does not say participants are paid. A discount program exists for low-income families.

who_can_apply: Must be 15 when you apply. Must pass the swim test. Must be free to work all of June and July.
how_to_apply: Sign up for a swim test at tucsonparks.info/lifeguardfallswimtest. The page gives no other form. If you have questions, send an email to cotlifeguard@tucsonaz.gov or call 520-837-8119.
notes: The page shows 2026 in its footer, so the dates are likely fall 2026, but confirm. Swim test: 300 yard front crawl, 50 yard approach stroke with rescue tube, treading water, 50 yard side stroke with a dummy, 10 lb brick retrieval.
duration: Starguard class days listed on the page, then June and July work
pay_detail: Starts at $16.75 per hour

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 17.
how_to_apply: Fill out the volunteer application form (PDF on the page) and give it to the library branch where you want to volunteer. The library contacts you if there is an opening.
notes: The application PDF on the page is labeled 2024. Openings depend on each branch, so ask staff.
duration: Not stated. Teens track hours with a log.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 21. The page lists no other rules.
how_to_apply: Apply online at summeryouth.pima.gov. Or pick up a paper form at high schools and community centers in Pima County.
notes: Expect applications to open again in early 2027 (last year it was February). Check the page in January.
duration: Two 2026 sessions: June 1 to June 26, or July 6 to July 31
pay_detail: Minimum $16.54 per hour (2026)

who_can_apply: Teens entering 9th through 12th grade.
how_to_apply: Use the zoo volunteer application when it reopens in January 2027, with the teen's own email and phone number. The page gives no direct Zoo Crew link. Call (520) 791-3204 with questions.
notes: Applications are closed now. Teens should be their own main contact with the zoo.
duration: About 4 hours a month for a year, plus a required 4-day training. After one year you must be invited back.
pay_detail: Unpaid. No fee listed on the page.

who_can_apply: Currently in high school, 16 or older by June 7, 2027, a U.S. citizen or permanent resident, and lived in Arizona at least one year.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. It has 4 essay questions. Add a signed student and parent agreement. Add 2 recommenders. One must be a science teacher. Their letters are due Jan 7. Add an unofficial transcript.
notes: Both recommendations must be in by Jan 7. If not, your form will not be looked at.
duration: 7 weeks, June 7 to July 23, 2027
pay_detail: No cost to participate. A stipend is not mentioned. Earns 3 units of MCB credit.

who_can_apply: High school students, especially juniors. They come from backgrounds that are hard in money, school or social ways. You need a 3.0 GPA, 2 recommendation letters, a science fair or research example, U.S. citizenship or a permanent visa, and a Social Security number.
how_to_apply: Send in the form with a 1 to 2 page essay. The essay topic is "Why I love science and what the summer medical research apprenticeship will mean to me". The page points to ignorance.medicine.arizona.edu for more but does not give the steps.
notes: Applicants must have a Social Security number. Dates and deadline are not posted. Contact the College of Medicine to confirm.
duration: Length not stated
pay_detail: Federal minimum hourly wage, 40 hours a week for the length of the program

who_can_apply: Arizona teens ages 12 to 18 (grades 7 to 12). You must be 12 by Sept 30, 2026. You must come to monthly meetings and do at least 10 extra volunteer hours each semester.
how_to_apply: Sign up in ZSuites and fill out the Google form. A parent or caregiver and the teen both go to the info meeting. It is required. Questions: Alex Kolnacki, akolnacki@arizona.edu.
notes: Meetings are at the Big Farm, 2201 E. Roger Rd. The page says the program started in 2012.
duration: School year. Meetings are the first Thursday of the month, 5:30 to 7:00 PM, dinner provided.
pay_detail: $20 state and county 4-H fee at registration. Programming is mostly free or low cost.

who_can_apply: Camps are for youth ages 5 to 18. The page does not give an age rule for teen counselors. Ask the camp coordinator.
how_to_apply: Counselor applications open March 1, 2027 at noon on the camps page. Email the Camp Coordinator Moonie with questions.
notes: Applications for camper scholarships and sign-up open the same day. The page does not say if counselor jobs are paid.
duration: Summer camps (over 35 camps a year)
pay_detail: Not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Students entering grades 9 to 12 in El Paso or Pueblo counties. You must be first in your family to go to college, low income, or tied to the military.
how_to_apply: Apply online when the link opens at the end of January 2027.
notes: Students entering grades 11 and 12 can take a dual enrollment course for 3.0 college credits at no cost, Monday to Friday afternoons 1 to 3:30 PM during June. The program has run since 1987.
duration: Multi-year program. Summer Academic Institute runs during June.
pay_detail: Free to students. No pay.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 and up at the University of Colorado Hospital. It is in Aurora. The same goes for Highlands Ranch. It also goes for Broomfield and Steadman Hawkins Clinic Denver. Other places have other minimum ages.
how_to_apply: Use the online application for the hospital you want. The Aurora hospital link is on the program page. Requirements differ by hospital, so check with the hospital first.
notes: Job shadowing at UCHealth is for ages 18 and older. The volunteer page does not list a summer teen program. Ask the hospital about other teen options.
duration: Most locations ask for 65 hours or a steady six months.
pay_detail: Unpaid

who_can_apply: Current 8th graders who will start high school in the fall and are first-generation college students (no parent finished college in the U.S.). No minimum GPA. Plan to join for all 4 years.
how_to_apply: Apply online with essay answers. A committee picks students.
notes: The page text looks old (it lists a May 30, 2022 deadline). Email or call before you plan around it. For 8th graders only, so it is for students about to start 9th grade.
duration: 4 years. Two weeks of summer camp each year.
pay_detail: Free. Lunch and rides are provided. A one-time $15 registration fee is due if you are accepted (tell the team if that is a problem).

who_can_apply: 4-H youth in 9th to 12th grade. Adults also attend.
how_to_apply: Register on Zsuite (4h.zsuite.org). Questions: contact the Utah 4-H State Office at 435-797-4444 or your county 4-H office.
notes: Held with Rep. Joel Briscoe and the Office of Legislative Research.
duration: 1 day (2026: April 22, 9 AM to 3 PM)
pay_detail: $25 per person (includes t-shirt and lunch).

who_can_apply: All teens in grades 9 to 12 (those who have finished 8th grade).
how_to_apply: Sign-up for the 2027 Teen Summit will open in summer 2027. Contact Vernon Parent at vernon.parent@usu.edu or 385-468-4832.
notes: A youth waiver is needed. Check the page for the cost when registration opens.
duration: 3 days (July 12 to 14, 2027)
pay_detail: Cost not posted yet.

who_can_apply: Utah teens in grades 9 to 12. A waiver must be uploaded in Zsuite when you register.
how_to_apply: Sign up through Zsuite and upload the signed waiver. Teens in grades 10 to 12 can also apply to the Teen Winter Retreat Design Team, which has 8 spots. Apply by Oct 24 with a 4-H portfolio, which is a resume and cover letter, and short answers.
notes: Design Team applications are open Sept 1 to Oct 24 and let teens plan activities and teach workshops. Questions: Utah 4-H State Office, 435-797-4444.
duration: Friday 4 PM to Saturday 3 PM (Jan 22 to 23, 2027)
pay_detail: $135 per person. Includes lodging, meals and activities.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 5 to 18 in any Utah county. Find your county office to sign up.
how_to_apply: Use the Find your County Office link on the Utah 4-H site, then ask that office how to join. Registration for state events is through Zsuite.
notes: State events include Teen Summit, Teen Winter Retreat and Mock Legislature. Fees and dates differ by county and event. Ask your county office.
duration: Ongoing
pay_detail: Not stated on the page. Ask your county office about fees.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 24. The apply page says the help is for youth who are out of school and struggling to connect to work or school, or who struggle at school or work. A counselor decides if you qualify.
how_to_apply: Apply online or at a local Employment Center. A counselor contacts you within three business days. You then send the papers they ask for within 45 days. Together you make a job plan.
notes: This is a state program with eligibility checks, so not every teen qualifies. You need a Utah ID account to apply online. The program page does not say which employers or pay rates are used.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: The page says paid internships. The pay rate is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: You must be at least 14 when you finish the application. Some jobs have other age rules. You need a valid email address.
how_to_apply: Fill out one online application. List other jobs you would take as backups. Read the employee rules before you apply. You can call Employee Services at 801-451-8058 for help.
notes: Lagoon is in Farmington, Utah. Perks include free entry to Lagoon Family Days and park store discounts. The park uses E-Verify to check work eligibility. A separate job page covers the fall Frightmares season.
duration: Seasonal. Dates are not stated on the program page.
pay_detail: Pay is called competitive. The rate is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Students with disabilities ages 14 through 21 (or age 22 while in special education services). You must be in a high school or after high school program. You must be eligible for IDEA services. Or you have a disability under section 504. You do not have to be a client of Vocational Rehabilitation.
how_to_apply: Contact your school Vocational Rehabilitation liaison or a local VR office. You can send an email to vrtransition@utah.gov. You can also call 801-887-9500.
notes: Every public high school and charter school has a VR counselor. Contractors check that a student fits before services start.
duration: Varies by student
pay_detail: Instruction by community partners is free.

who_can_apply: Incoming 9th to 12th graders enrolled in an approved agriculture class for the next school year, with an approved SAE plan. High school graduates are not eligible. Your school must run a Summer Ag Program.
how_to_apply: Talk to your high school agriculture teacher. You need an approved SAE plan in the Agricultural Experience Tracker (AET). Use your boundary school's Summer Ag Program. If that is not available, you can work with a school in the same district with parent consent and approval.
notes: The guide is written for teachers and districts. Each program needs at least 35 students and a licensed ag teacher, so not every school has one. Ask your ag teacher.
duration: Starts the day after the school contract ends and runs to the day before the next one starts
pay_detail: The program itself is school based. Projects can be paid or unpaid, and your employer may pay you for SAE work. School credit may be offered.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 18.
how_to_apply: Use the Register link on the program page. The page does not list the steps.
notes: You also get help with your resume and may be placed in a job at the Y. The page does not list locations, so ask your nearest Y.
duration: 8 weeks, flexible
pay_detail: Not stated on the program page. Cost is not listed either.

who_can_apply: Youth and young adults ages 14 to 24.
how_to_apply: Call 303-271-4755 or schedule an appointment with a Career Coach on the page.
notes: The page says the Governor's Summer Job Hunt is a free program for ages 14 to 24. Job Corps (ages 16 to 24) is also listed: 303-623-0420. Office: 3500 Illinois St, Suite 1600, Golden, CO.
duration: Ongoing
pay_detail: Services are free. The page says it connects people to paid and unpaid work experience.
